title: ⚡ How to Optimize React Application Performance?
excerpt: Everything works fine initially, but as the application grows, pages become slower and interactions feel less responsive.
body:
ㅤ 📘 Engineering Notes | From Concepts to Code — Post 12 ㅤ Imagine building an e-commerce application using React. Everything works fine initially, but as the application grows, pages become slower and interactions feel less responsive. Why does this happen? 🤔 One possible reason is unnecessary rendering and expensive operations. Let's explore 5 ways to improve React performance! 👇 ㅤ 1️⃣ 𝗔𝘃𝗼𝗶𝗱 𝗨𝗻𝗻𝗲𝗰𝗲𝘀𝘀𝗮𝗿𝘆 𝗥𝗲-𝗥𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀 🔄 React components can re-render when their state or parent changes. React.memo can help skip re-renders when component props remain unchanged. Example: const ProductCard = React.memo(function ProductCard({ product }) { return

{product.name}

; }); ✅ Useful for components that render frequently with unchanged props. ㅤ 2️⃣ 𝗨𝘀𝗲 𝘂𝘀𝗲𝗠𝗲𝗺𝗼 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗘𝘅𝗽𝗲𝗻𝘀𝗶𝘃𝗲 𝗖𝗮𝗹𝗰𝘂𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 🧠 Imagine filtering thousands of products. Without optimization, filtering may run again during unrelated re-renders. Example: const filteredProducts = useMemo( () => products.filter(p => p.price < 100), [products] ); useMemo caches the calculated result until its dependencies change. ✅ Helpful when calculations are expensive. ㅤ 3️⃣ 𝗨𝘀𝗲 𝘂𝘀𝗲𝗖𝗮𝗹𝗹𝗯𝗮𝗰𝗸 𝗪𝗵𝗲𝗻 𝗡𝗲𝗲𝗱𝗲𝗱 🎯 useCallback caches a function reference between renders. This can help memoized child components avoid unnecessary re-renders when receiving function props. 💡 Not every function needs useCallback. ㅤ 4️⃣ 𝗨𝘀𝗲 𝗟𝗮𝘇𝘆 𝗟𝗼𝗮𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 📦 Instead of loading all component code immediately, we can load certain components when needed. Example: const Dashboard = React.lazy(() => import('./Dashboard')); ✅ Reduces initial JavaScript loading ✅ Useful for large application sections ✅ Helps improve initial load performance ㅤ 5️⃣ 𝗢𝗽𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗶𝘇𝗲 𝗟𝗮𝗿𝗴𝗲 𝗟𝗶𝘀𝘁𝘀 📊 Rendering thousands of items at once can slow down the interface. List virtualization renders only the items needed for the visible area. ✅ Less DOM work ✅ Smoother scrolling ✅ Better performance with large lists ㅤ 💡 𝗠𝘆 𝗞𝗲𝘆 𝗧𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗮𝘄𝗮𝘆 React performance isn't about adding useMemo or useCallback everywhere. It's about identifying actual bottlenecks and applying the right optimization. Tools like React DevTools Profiler help us measure performance before making changes. 🚀 Measure first. Optimize what matters. ㅤ 💬 Which React performance optimization technique do you use most often? ㅤ #ReactJS #WebPerformance #SoftwareEngineering #FrontendDevelopment #JavaScript
